`@synap-core/sdk` is a typed tRPC client for a Synap pod. Every procedure the pod exposes is available with
autocomplete and compile-time checks, because the client is typed with the pod's own router type.

The SDK calls the pod's `/trpc` endpoint, which accepts only a **sign-in session**: a person's session cookie in the
browser, or their session token anywhere else. It is for apps that act as a signed-in person. It does not take API
keys: for a script, an integration or an agent that holds an API key, use the
[Hub REST API](#scripts-and-agents-with-an-api-key) instead.

## What you need

- A pod: [hosted](/docs/start/cloud-quickstart) or [self-hosted](/docs/start/self-host-quickstart).
- An account on it you can sign in with.
- The ID of the workspace you want to read.

## 1. Install

```bash
npm install @synap-core/sdk
```

For a React app, install the React bindings instead; they include the SDK:

```bash
npm install @synap-core/react
```

## 2. Sign in and create a client

In the browser, on a subdomain of the pod's domain (for example `app.example.com` next to `pod.example.com`) where
the person is already signed in, pass no credential: every request is sent with `credentials: "include"`, so the
browser's session cookie authenticates it.

```ts
import { createSynapClient } from "@synap-core/sdk";

const synap = createSynapClient({
  podUrl: "https://pod.example.com", // no trailing slash, no /trpc
  workspaceId,
});
```

Anywhere else (a server, a script, a desktop or mobile app), sign in once to get a session token, and pass it as
`sessionToken`. A pod with password sign-in issues one through the native login flow of its sign-in service:

```bash
FLOW=$(curl -fsS https://pod.example.com/.ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/api | jq -r .id)
curl -fsS -X POST "https://pod.example.com/.ory/kratos/public/self-service/login?flow=$FLOW" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method": "password", "identifier": "you@example.com", "password": "<your password>"}' \
  | jq -r .session_token
```

```ts
const synap = createSynapClient({
  podUrl: "https://pod.example.com",
  sessionToken: process.env.SYNAP_SESSION_TOKEN,
  workspaceId: process.env.SYNAP_WORKSPACE_ID!,
  onAuthError: () => {
    // 401: the session expired or was revoked. Sign in again.
  },
});
```

A session lasts 30 days and is not extended by use; treat the token like a password.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `podUrl` | Base URL of the pod. The client calls `<podUrl>/trpc`. |
| `sessionToken` | A sign-in session token, sent as `x-session-token`. Leave it out to use the browser's session cookie. |
| `workspaceId` | Sent as `x-workspace-id` to scope requests. Pass `""` for procedures that need no workspace. |
| `extraHeaders` | Added to every request. |
| `onAuthError` | Called on `401`. The client then rejects with a clean tRPC error instead of a parse error. |

The type also has an `apiKey` option. It is only for the desktop app's local pod; a pod refuses API keys
(`synap_user_…`, `synap_hub_…`) on `/trpc` with `401`.

Calls made in the same tick are batched into one HTTP request, and values are encoded with superjson, which is why
plain HTTP clients should use the [Hub REST API](/docs/reference/hub-api) instead of `/trpc`.

## 3. Read entities

```ts
const { items, pagination } = await synap.entities.list.query({ limit: 20 });

for (const entity of items) {
  console.log(entity.id, entity.title);
}
```

`entities.list` takes `limit` (1 to 1000, default 50) and `offset`, and filters such as `profileSlug` (one kind, for
example `"task"`) and `facetSlug` (one role). With a workspace set, it returns that workspace's entities.

## 4. Write, and expect proposals

```ts
const result = await synap.entities.create.mutate({
  profileSlug: "note",
  title: "My first note",
});
```

Writes go through the pod's governance. Depending on who the key belongs to and the rules you set, a write is applied
directly or comes back as a **proposal** (`status: "proposed"` with a `proposalId`) that a person approves. Handle
both. See [Validation policy](/docs/build/concepts/validation-policy).

## React

```tsx
import { SynapProvider, useSynap } from "@synap-core/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <SynapProvider podUrl="https://pod.example.com" workspaceId={workspaceId}>
      <Entities />
    </SynapProvider>
  );
}

function Entities() {
  const { data } = useSynap.entities.list.useQuery({ limit: 20 });
  return <ul>{data?.items.map((e) => <li key={e.id}>{e.title}</li>)}</ul>;
}
```

`useSynap` is the tRPC React client itself, not a function: write `useSynap.entities.list.useQuery(…)`, not
`useSynap()`. `SynapProvider` takes the same options as `createSynapClient` (here, the signed-in person's session
cookie; pass `sessionToken` outside the browser), plus an optional `queryClient` to share an existing TanStack Query
client.

`@synap-core/react` also exports ready-made `RouterInputs` and `RouterOutputs` types, `useSynapContext` (the provider's
`podUrl` and `workspaceId`), and the hooks `useEntity`, `useEntities`, `useLinks` and `useView`.

## Package reference

| Package | Exports |
|---|---|
| `@synap-core/sdk` | `createSynapClient`, and the types `SynapClient`, `SynapClientOptions` and `AppRouter` |
| `@synap-core/react` | `SynapProvider`, `useSynap`, `useSynapContext`, `useEntity`, `useEntities`, `useLinks`, `useView`, and the types `RouterInputs`, `RouterOutputs`, `SynapProviderProps`, `AppRouter` |

Both packages ship ES modules and CommonJS with TypeScript declarations, under the MIT license. The router types
come from `@synap-core/api-types`, a dependency, so the client's types follow the version of that package you install.
Use only what the package root exports: other subpaths are not part of the published API.

## Scripts and agents with an API key

An [API key](/docs/build/api-keys) works on the Hub REST API under `/api/hub`, not on `/trpc`. From TypeScript,
[`@synap-core/hub-rest-client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@synap-core/hub-rest-client) is a zero-dependency
client for it:

```bash
npm install @synap-core/hub-rest-client
```

```ts
import { HubRestClient } from "@synap-core/hub-rest-client";

const hub = new HubRestClient({
  podUrl: "https://pod.example.com",
  apiKey: process.env.SYNAP_API_KEY!,
  workspaceId: process.env.SYNAP_WORKSPACE_ID,
});

const entities = await hub.getRecentEntities({ profileSlug: "task", limit: 20 });
```

From any other language, call the same routes over HTTP with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`:

```bash
curl "https://pod.example.com/api/hub/entities?profileSlug=task&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNAP_API_KEY"
```

Every route is in the [Hub REST API reference](/docs/reference/hub-api).
